title: Stone Town on Foot: A Walking Guide
excerpt: Stone Town is a maze of narrow alleys, carved doors and old merchant houses. A walking guide for your first day.
body:
Stone Town is the historic heart of Zanzibar City and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its architecture blends Swahili, Arab, Indian and European influences.

## The best way to explore

On foot, ideally with a local guide for the first hours. Stone Town's alleys are confusing, and a guide brings the history to life.

## Highlights

- **Carved doors:** often with brass studs and detailed patterns.
- **Old Fort:** built in the late 17th century.
- **House of Wonders:** an iconic building on the seafront (check whether it is open; it has been under restoration).
- **Former slave market:** now the site of the Anglican cathedral and a memorial. A sobering and important visit.
- **Darajani Market:** spices, fruit, fish and daily life.
- **[Forodhani Gardens](/blog/forodhani-night-market/):** night food market.

## Tips

- Start early or late afternoon to avoid the heat.
- Dress modestly: shoulders and knees covered.
- Ask before photographing people.

## Where to eat

See [where and what to eat in Stone Town](/blog/stone-town-food-guide/).

## How long

One or two nights. See [how many days on Zanzibar](/blog/how-many-days-zanzibar/).
